notes: 18 cases: 10 positive / 8 negative. By origin: 6 golden (authored), 6 real-trace (byte-verbatim production user turns: 4 positive + 2 NEGATIVE), 6 negative (authored near-misses). skillify is a rank-6 skill by measured usage — exactly 4 invocations across 4 distinct sessions, re-counted this session by parsing every UUID-named transcript under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-broomva-broomva/ and walking each assistant event's tool_use blocks: exactly 4 files carry a Skill tool_use with input.skill == 'skillify'. All four are carried here as real-trace positives (verification_log.real_trace_verbatim names the transcript, line, message uuid and timestamp for each). The two real-trace NEGATIVES are the finding this set is proudest of: production turns that contain the literal string '/skillify' and in which the skill correctly did NOT fire — non-firing re-proven this session the same way, by enumerating every Skill tool_use in both files. checkit's pilot recorded 'no_production_sourced_negative' as a known gap; for skillify that gap is closed, because this user routinely names the verb inside a subordinate clause while the imperative asks for something else. CORRECTION 2026-07-28 — this paragraph used to continue: 'AUTHORED CASES CARRY NO TRIGGER PHRASE AND NEVER THE WORD skillify. That is deliberate and it is where the paraphrase-inference measurement lives: every USE WHEN entry in the description except one (package this as a skill) contains the skill's own name, so a golden built on a USE WHEN entry would measure string matching.' The second half of that is FALSE, and it was load-bearing — it justified a coverage gap. Counted this session directly off the frontmatter: USE WHEN carries six quoted entries plus one unquoted trailing clause. Exactly TWO contain the skill's name — 'skillify it' and 'skillify this'. Four quoted entries do not: 'package this as a skill', 'distill this into a skill', 'make this a skill', 'turn this into a skill'; nor does the tail, 'or at the end of an ad-hoc workflow that worked and should become permanent'. The only true version of the old claim is the narrower one that all six QUOTED entries contain the substring 'skill'. The first half does survive as a fact about this file: the six authored positives contain neither 'skillify' nor 'skill' (verified per prompt; the authored negatives negative-03 and negative-04 do contain 'skill'/'skills', which is the point of those two). But it is now a CHOICE with an unpaid cost rather than a forced constraint — four literal USE WHEN phrases were available that leak no name, and none is exercised. Recorded as known_gaps.no_literal_trigger_phrase_case, not as a justification. The real traces are exempt from the paraphrase rule: production evidence keeps its own phrasing, and all six contain '/skillify'. Expect the validator to emit six 'prompt contains the literal skill name' warnings, one per real-trace case (re-confirmed: 'skillify' occurs in exactly those 6 of 18 prompts); they are warnings, not errors, and they are correct about what those six cases measure — that the trigger surface fires, and on the two negatives that it does not fire on the string alone. EVERY case is satisfiable in the runner's clean temp workspace: runner._materialize_present copies the skill dir to <cwd>/.claude/skills/skillify with evals/ and tests/ removed by SKILL_COPY_EXCLUDE and nothing else installed — no git, no branch, no PRs, no knowledge graph, no docs/. scripts/skillify_check.py IS present, so the agent can genuinely run the gate. connects_to_active_work is now asserted on NO case: it was on golden-01 and was dropped this session with measured evidence — see known_gaps.checks_deliberately_unused.connects_to_active_work. Register: no em dash appears in any prompt in this file, authored or production — re-checked this session across all 18.

execution_contract.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object; it is here so the intended contract is reviewable and so drift between intent and CLI flags is visible. Values mirror runner.py's module constants read at authoring time (DEFAULT_TRIALS, DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, DEFAULT_CASE_THRESHOLD, DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S).
execution_contract.workspace: clean temp dir per trial; skill installed at .claude/skills/skillify; --setting-sources project; --permission-mode bypassPermissions; --no-session-persistence. SKILL_COPY_EXCLUDE removes evals/ (the answer key) and tests/, so scripts/skillify_check.py IS present in the case workspace and the agent can genuinely run the gate.
execution_contract.negative_semantics: runner.grade_trial computes run_checks(case.expected_checks, ctx) for EVERY trial and attaches the results to the TrialResult, and only then branches. On a should_trigger:false trial the branch is `if triggered: return out(FAIL, 'over-triggered on a near-miss prompt', ...)` — returned without consulting the check outcomes, so the checks listed on a negative can neither create nor rescue that verdict. (CORRECTION: this field previously said the checks are consulted 'BEFORE' — imprecise. They DO run; they simply do not gate.) They are additive assertions about what the agent did INSTEAD of firing — they stop the case from resting on the non-trigger alone. On the 8 negatives here that additive content is final_answer_non_empty and nothing else; see check_semantics.no_permission_denials.
execution_contract.positive_semantics: Symmetrically, a should_trigger:true trial that never fired returns RECOVERED when transcript.read_skill_content() is true (the agent answered by reading .claude/skills/skillify/SKILL.md off disk) and FAIL otherwise; in both branches the check results are attached but `failed` is not consulted, and TrialResult.passed is `outcome == PASS`, so RECOVERED is not a pass. skill_triggered, where listed, is therefore REDUNDANT with control flow and appears only on the two cases whose sole substantive claim is triggering, so that claim is legible in this file instead of living only in grade_trial. It is documentation, not discrimination, and the rationales say so.

known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks: Four assertions this set would make if it could. They have no CHECK_REGISTRY entry and are NOT referenced anywhere above, because an unknown id is a hard PromptSetError that makes the whole file unloadable. (1) skill_not_triggered — a positive-form assertion that the skill stayed quiet, so a negative's central claim appears in expected_checks rather than only in grade_trial's control flow. (2) produces_a_skill_contract — asserts the written artifact is a SKILL.md with name/description/triggers frontmatter, which is what would separate 'wrote a markdown file' from 'authored a skill contract'; documents_finding is the closest available proxy and it is strictly weaker (and, per check_semantics, has a skill-specific false-fail on top). (3) states_latent_deterministic_split — SKILL.md pipeline step 1 requires the split be stated in one line before scaffolding, and that is the single most skill-specific observable behaviour in the whole procedure; traverses_to_primitives is a loose proxy for it, and check_semantics records just how loose. (4) no_unrequested_pipeline — asserts the agent did NOT run a 10-step distillation over a bounded request, the over-delivery failure mode every negative here is really about. Until (4) exists the negatives assert non-trigger plus final_answer_non_empty, not absence-of-over-delivery — and 'answer-health' in this file means final_answer_non_empty alone, since no_permission_denials cannot fail on agent behaviour (check_semantics).
known_gaps.no_audit_branch_case: SKILL.md §Scope (line 179) lists 'auditing an existing skill against the 10-step bar' as IN scope, and the target line says target may be 'an existing skill dir to audit'. No case tests that branch, deliberately. The frontmatter description — which is what actually drives triggering, and what this harness measures — never offers auditing as a reason to invoke: its USE WHEN list is entirely about distilling a session, and 'TESTED, registered' describes the output. CORRECTION 2026-07-28: this entry used to say the description 'never mentions auditing'. It does mention it once — 'script-test gate (bstack skills audit --require-tests)' — but as a pipeline STEP the skill runs, never as a trigger, which is the distinction that matters and the one the old wording overstated. A positive built on the audit branch would grade the model against a rule its trigger surface does not state, and a negative would be worse. Stated as a gap rather than papered over, with a suggested skill fix below.
known_gaps.no_bstack_primitive_negative: The sharpest available near-miss was built and then discarded: 'this has come up three times now, branch-before-edit should be a hard gate not a habit, promote it.' SKILL.md §Scope explicitly carves it out (lines 181-182: 'promoting a bstack *primitive* (that's the bstack-engine rule-of-three, user-initiated)'), so the label would have been defensible from the SKILL BODY. It is not defensible from the DESCRIPTION, whose NOT-FOR clause reads in full: 'ingesting an external artifact (use /checkit); retrospective "what have I done repeatedly" discovery alone (use the look-back lens); a one-off task with no reusable procedure' — no primitive carve-out. Grading a model against a carve-out that exists only below the trigger surface measures document divergence, not routing. Same reasoning as no_audit_branch_case; same suggested fix.

known_gaps.single_authored_positive_shape: All six authored positives share one shape — a procedure that already worked, stated inline, plus a request for permanence. That is the description's own dominant USE WHEN clause and it is where the skill's real traffic sits, but it means the set does NOT probe an authored positive with a genuinely ambiguous referent ('make that permanent' with nothing named). Such a prompt is unanswerable in a clean temp workspace, so the omission is environmental, not an oversight: real-trace-01 is the closest thing to it in the set, and its checks are narrowed for exactly that reason. Read together with no_literal_trigger_phrase_case, the two describe the same hole from two sides — every authored positive is a paraphrase of one clause.
known_gaps.suggested_skill_fix: Two lines in the frontmatter description would let this set grow the two cases it currently refuses to write. (1) Extend USE WHEN with an audit trigger, e.g. 'or auditing an existing skill against the 10-step bar' — SKILL.md §Scope line 179 already claims it, so this is bringing the trigger surface up to the body, not adding scope. (2) Extend NOT FOR with the primitive carve-out, e.g. 'promoting a bstack primitive (rule-of-three, user-initiated)' — again already in §Scope, lines 181-182. Neither changes behaviour the skill does not already document; both make it measurable. Separately, and outside this skill: scoping transcript._skill_content_patterns pattern 1 to the skill under test would remove the documents_finding false-fail this set has to work around.
known_gaps.no_literal_trigger_phrase_case: OPEN, and newly honest as of 2026-07-28. No case in this set uses any of the four literal USE WHEN phrases that do NOT contain the skill's own name — 'package this as a skill', 'distill this into a skill', 'make this a skill', 'turn this into a skill'. The set previously justified that by asserting those entries would leak the skill's name; counted against the frontmatter this session they do not, and only 'skillify it' and 'skillify this' do. So the set measures two bands and skips a third: paraphrase inference with no trigger vocabulary at all (the six goldens, none of which contains 'skill' or 'skillify') and the production trigger surface with the name present (the six real traces). The untested middle band — a literal, name-free USE WHEN phrase — is precisely the band a description edit is most likely to break silently, because it is the wording a user copies out of the docs. Closing it means adding a case; this revision was scoped to prose and check selection and added none.
known_gaps.documents_finding_false_fail: OPEN. documents_finding is the primary outcome assertion on 8 of the 10 positives (golden-01 through golden-06, real-trace-03, real-trace-04), and its tool arm has a skill-SPECIFIC false-fail: a Write to <cwd>/.claude/skills/<newskill>/SKILL.md — the most natural destination for a newly distilled skill in the runner's workspace, and the destination skillify's own step 10 dogfoods — is dropped by transcript.refers_to_skill_content before _DOC_PATH_RE is ever consulted, because pattern 1 of _skill_content_patterns is the bare \.claude[/\\]+skills[/\\] with no skill-name component. Mechanism and measured cases: check_semantics.documents_finding. The set does not paper over it — the text arm rescues the common narration, and the eight rationales now describe what the check does rather than what it was assumed to do — but the residual is real: a correct run that writes into .claude/skills/ AND narrates tersely fails a check it should pass. The clean fix is upstream, in transcript._skill_content_patterns: scope pattern 1 to '.claude/skills/<skill-under-test>/' rather than to '.claude/skills/', which would also stop any other skill-authoring skill hitting the same wall. Not attempted here; this file does not own checks.py or transcript.py.

check_semantics.documents_finding: check_documents_finding = _document_tool_evidence(ctx) OR _hit(_DOCUMENT_RE, ctx.text). CORRECTION: this set previously described the tool arm as '_DOC_PATH_RE matches a Write to any *.md'. That is wrong about the mechanism. _document_tool_evidence iterates _candidate_tool_uses(ctx) — which FIRST drops every tool_use whose JSON-serialised input satisfies transcript.refers_to_skill_content(skill, blob, workspace) — then keeps only tu.name in _WRITE_TOOLS {Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit}, then takes _target(tu) (the first non-empty value among _TARGET_KEYS, i.e. file_path for a Write), and only then applies _DOC_PATH_RE to that target STRING. _DOC_PATH_RE is never reached for an excluded call. SKILL-SPECIFIC FALSE-FAIL, which is why this matters here and not in other sets: pattern 1 of transcript._skill_content_patterns is the bare regex \.claude[/\\]+skills[/\\] with NO skill-name component, so it fires on ANY path under .claude/skills/ — including a brand-new, differently-named skill. skillify's entire deliverable is a new skill, and its own SKILL.md step 10 dogfoods an install to ~/.claude/skills/<name>/. Measured 2026-07-28 on constructed transcripts: Write{file_path: '/tmp/ws/.claude/skills/worktree-unjam/SKILL.md'} → excluded → tool arm returns ''; Write{file_path: 'skills/worktree-unjam/SKILL.md'} (SKILL.md step 9's canonical monorepo layout) → not excluded → tool arm returns 'Write(skills/worktree-unjam/SKILL.md)'. transcript.py's own docstring states the assumption that makes the exclusion sound — 'the workspace holds exactly one skill by construction' — which is true at setup (runner._materialize_present copies exactly one skill) and false the moment skillify succeeds. The text arm usually rescues it: 'I created .claude/skills/worktree-unjam/SKILL.md with the four-step procedure.' matches _DOCUMENT_RE (a verb from wrote|writing|written to|filed|saved|created|documented|note at|captured in|recorded in, then within 80 non-newline chars a .md/.json/.ya?ml/research//docs//notes?//entit(y|ies)). Measured: the SAME correct write narrated tersely, with no doc path in the prose, FAILS both arms. Not vacuous in the other direction either — measured: a run that produces no write and only describes what it would write also fails both arms. Net: a real assertion with a real, skill-specific false-fail whose size depends on where the agent writes and how it narrates. Tracked as known_gaps.documents_finding_false_fail.
check_semantics.no_permission_denials: RUN-HEALTH SENTINEL, NOT BEHAVIOURAL COVERAGE — stated plainly because this set asserts it on 11 of 18 cases. runner.LiveRunner.build_argv appends '--permission-mode bypassPermissions' unconditionally, and check_no_permission_denials reads transcript.permission_denials, which is the result event's permission_denials array. With permissions bypassed that array is empty on any healthy run, so the check cannot fail on anything the agent CHOSE to do — only on a sandbox or harness anomaly, which is the one thing it is worth keeping for. On the 8 negatives, whose expected_checks are [final_answer_non_empty, no_permission_denials], it is PADDING: those cases' substantive content is grade_trial's non-trigger branch plus final_answer_non_empty. It is never the only meaningful check on a case, because final_answer_non_empty is a genuine predicate (below), but nothing in this file should be read as claiming no_permission_denials contributes behavioural signal.
check_semantics.final_answer_non_empty: A real predicate, not a formality. It grades transcript.final_text() — the result event's result string — and fails on an empty answer, on fewer than _MIN_ANSWER_WORDS (3) words, or on an _STUB_RE acknowledgement. Measured 2026-07-28: 'Done.' → FAIL (acknowledgement only), 'ok' → FAIL, 'Yes, that is worth keeping as a skill.' → PASS (8 words / 38 chars).
check_semantics.produces_ranked_next_steps: Requires BOTH: ≥2 lines matching _ENUM_RE (a line beginning with `N.`/`N)`/`-`/`*`/`•`) AND one hit of _NEXT_STEP_RE (next step|next action|recommend|suggest|option \d|i'd start|priorit), measured over ctx.text (assistant text + final result), not over the closing turn alone. Measured 2026-07-28: 'Done. I wrote the fixture-refresh skill to skills/fixture-refresh/SKILL.md.' → FAIL; a two-bullet summary of what the run ALREADY DID that happens to contain 'I recommend this layout.' → PASS; an honest 'Remaining next steps: 1. run the resolver eval 2. register in the monorepo README' → PASS. So it separates 'wrote a file and stopped' from 'wrote a file and enumerated something', but it does NOT verify that what was enumerated is remaining work. Rationales that implied otherwise have been corrected.
check_semantics.traverses_to_primitives: A single hit of _PRIMITIVE_RE (under the hood|underneath|primitive|mechanism|implement(ed|ation|s)|how it (actually )?works|built on|relies on|boils down to|the reason (it|this)|architectur\w+|substrate) anywhere in ctx.text. The 'implement(ed|ation|s)' alternative makes it cheap for this skill in particular. Measured 2026-07-28: 'I implemented the release-notes skill as a single SKILL.md describing all four steps in prose' — the undifferentiated-blob failure golden-04's rationale used to claim this check catches — PASSES on 'implemented'. It does still fail on a blob narrated with no mechanism vocabulary at all ('I wrote a skill that lists the release-notes steps: pull merge commits, group by ticket, drop chores.' → FAIL). Treat it as a weak proxy, which is what known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks item (3) already says.
check_semantics.skill_triggered: check_skill_triggered returns transcript.triggered(skill), the OR of detector A (a Skill tool_use naming the skill) and detector B (a top-level tool_use_result {success: true, commandName}). On a positive case grade_trial has already branched on that same value, so listing it changes no verdict. See execution_contract.positive_semantics.
